items.title: Will Ethiopia’s neighbours intervene as Tigray war escalates?
items.description: Tigray’s renewed war is testing Ethiopia’s already strained regional ties.

items.title: Pro-Iran groups behind foiled attack on Bank of America in Paris, FBI finds
items.description: According to information the FBI shared with French authorities, an Iraqi man linked to pro-Iran groups is suspected of having orchestrated a recent wave of attacks in Europe targeting American and Jewish sites, including the March 28 attempted terrorist attack. He was arrested by US authorities in Turkey.

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Thursday there would be a response to a Russian strike that hit two buses in the frontline city of Kramatorsk, killing 30 people and wounding 18 others. items.title: How the Houthi-Saudi conflict is affecting countries on Africa's Red Sea coast — and beyond
items.description: The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which Yemeni government forces are trying to take back from the Houthis, is located not far from Djibouti and other African states.

items.title: Trump Envoys in Talks With Putin’s Money Man Over Russian Gas, Reports Say
items.description: Senior US envoy Jared Kushner and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev have reportedly discussed bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream gas pipelines, five sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday, Oct. 8. items.title: Darfur: Healthcare needs outstrip resources as Security Council extends Sudan sanctions
items.description: More than 700,000 displaced people in Tawila, in Sudan’s war-ravaged Darfur region, face severe shortages of healthcare, food, water and protection, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Thursday as it called for an urgent increase in resources.

items.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine's public buses leave 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
items.description: Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than 4 1/2 years since Moscow's full-scale invasion.

items.title: Dozens Killed In Russian Strike On Passenger Buses In Kramatorsk
items.description: Dozens of people were killed in a Russian strike on the Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk on October 8, according to local authorities, a day after another deadly barrage killed at least 25 people across Ukraine.

items.title: EU Lifts Belarus-Related Sanctions on Russian Billionaire Gutseriev – RFE/RL
items.description: The billionaire remains subject to separate EU sanctions linked to Russia’s war in Ukraine.

items.title: 'Every day there is killing': Palestinians in Gaza face Israeli strikes despite ceasefire as peace deal stalls
items.description: Many Palestinians are still living in cramped tent cities, with the US plan to end the war largely stalled.

items.title: In Ukraine, holding on to childhood in a time of war
items.description: As war in Ukraine continues into its fifth year, some children have only known war. The Monitor revisits three young families striving to live full lives amid Russia’s military invasion.
